subject: Re: Urgent: sudden 5xx/429 spike — suspected retry amplification from ingestion cluster
messages:
From: Anna Park <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Collins <jared.collins@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: sudden 5xx/429 spike — top-level timeout/ingest failures

Hi Monica / Stephanie,

We're seeing a large increase in 5xx and 429 responses starting ~08:45 PDT from the ingestion cluster that talks to your hosted inference endpoints. Error rate climbed from ~0.3% -> 8% within 10 minutes; latency (p50/p95) also spiked and a subset of our workers are timing out.

Our preliminary logs show many repeated identical requests from the same API key (ak_nimbus-01) back-to-back, with no jitter between retries. Attached is a short sample (nimbus_request_sample.log) showing repeated requests and the corresponding 429/503 responses.

Questions:
- Can you confirm whether there were platform-side changes at ~08:40?
- Do you have per-key throttling or automated backoff that could be applied?

This is blocking some customer pipelines — our CTO is watching. Please advise ASAP.

Thanks,
Anna Park
Head of Platform Reliability, Nimbus Analytics
(attachment: nimbus_request_sample.log - text)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden 5xx/429 spike — top-level timeout/ingest failures

Hi Anna — thanks for the quick heads up and for the sample logs. We're treating this as a priority.

Quick context: no platform deployment was pushed at 08:40 from Redwood's side; we've got an active alert and I'm looping in Infra (Connor) and Sales leadership (Rishi) so we can coordinate an immediate mitigation and a short-term protection plan.

Immediate ask for your team: can you confirm whether your ingestion cluster recently updated any SDKs or changed retry configuration (timeouts, max attempts)? The pattern you sent (rapid identical retries) looks like a retry amplification loop rather than a server-side bug in isolation.

We'll come back with containment options in the next 30–60 minutes.

—Monica
Monica Patel | Account Lead, Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP_Nimbus_2JUL.pdf - pdf)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Anna Park <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden 5xx/429 spike — triage notes and recommended mitigations

Anna / Monica — quick triage from infra:

Summary of findings (08:45–09:30 window):
- Traffic originating from API key ak_nimbus-01 increased 6x and accounts for >70% of observed 429s and 503s.
- Request logs show tight retry loops: identical request bodies and no backoff/jitter between tries (intervals <200ms).
- Platform capacity was near steady-state; we saw localized connection saturation on a subset of serving nodes due to repeated replays, which pushed those nodes into transient overload and generated 5xx responses.

Likely cause: retry amplification from customer-side client or SDK default (immediate retries without exponential backoff or jitter) causing hot loops against the same route.

Short-term mitigations (can implement in ~5–15 minutes):
1) Apply a per-key soft rate limit for ak_nimbus-01 (throttle to parse/ingest rate) — protects other customers while we coordinate.
2) Introduce a 120s per-route circuit-breaker for repeated client retries (temporary, reversible).
3) Return Retry-After + 429 for short window to encourage backoff; we'll also add explicit header guidance.

Customer-side ask (recommended):
- Upgrade to Nimbus SDK 1.4.2 which defaults to exponential backoff + jitter (we validated with the Nimbus sample logs).
- If unable to upgrade immediately, change retry logic to max 3 attempts with randomized jitter 200–1000ms.

If you authorize the per-key throttle and circuit-breaker, we will apply them now and monitor for recovery.
Connor O'Brien
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: timeline_graph.png - image)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Anna Park <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: urgent escalation — executive summary & action plan (contains customer MAP)

Team / Anna — brief executive note:

Thanks for the rapid triage. Monica — please proceed with Connor's short-term mitigations immediately (per-key throttle + circuit-breaker). Priorities: protect overall platform, keep Nimbus informed, and avoid broad customer impact.

For Nimbus leadership: we propose a mutual action plan (attached) with three phases:
- Contain: Redwood applies targeted throttle + Retry-After headers (now).
- Remediate: Nimbus upgrades SDK to 1.4.2 or applies exponential backoff + jitter; coordinate a controlled restart of ingestion workers (within 2 hours).
- Prevent: Redwood to update our docs and default guidance, ship an SDK compatibility/observability check, and run a joint postmortem.

We're prepared to offer a small service credit for downtime during the window — we'll coordinate offline. Please confirm acceptance of the MAP timeline so we can move to contain.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales & Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: urgent escalation — status: contained and next steps

Hi Anna / Jared — quick update from Redwood: we applied the per-key soft throttle for ak_nimbus-01 at 12:15 PDT and enabled the temporary circuit-breaker. Within ~30 minutes we saw error rate fall from 8% -> 0.6% and latency returned to baseline. The dashboard link below shows the recovery curve.

Thank you for confirming that you're rolling the SDK patch and restarting a subset of workers — those changes matched our timeline and helped. Recommended next steps:
- Formal postmortem with joint timeline (we can schedule Tuesday 7/6).
- Redwood will change the hosted SDK docs and push a banner in the Console highlighting best-practice retry logic; infra will also add a per-key throttle option in the Console (Q3 work).
- We'll follow up about a goodwill credit — Marissa will own the finance coordination.

Links:
- Incident alert: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/INC-987654
- Recovery graph: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/teams/infra/keys/ak_nimbus-01
Again apologies for the disruption; appreciate the quick coordination.

—Monica Patel
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
